title: How Many Dragons to BEAT a Grandmaster?
summary: Tony (king + N Dragons) plays Latvian GM Arthur Neiksans ('arturchix', on webcam, full normal army) in ~5-minute online games, adding a dragon after each loss. Dragon = bishop + knight. 1 dragon: loss; 2 dragons: loss (~5:59); 3 dragons: win (~9:49), followed by courtesy rematches/role swaps where the GM also uses three dragons; the series continues upward and ends with Tony beating the GM with six dragons (~59:17).
rules: Player side: king + N Dragons only (N starts at 1). Opponent: full standard army.
Dragon moves like a bishop OR a knight (archbishop).
After each loss add one more dragon; continue (with rematches) until the dragon side beats the GM.
Normal chess otherwise; ~5-minute clocks ('There's only 5 minutes').
win_condition: Checkmate the grandmaster with king + dragons (final win used 6 dragons).

opponent.name: GM Arthur Neiksans (arturchix)
opponent.avatar_description: live webcam of a Latvian GM; account 'arturchix'

board.theme_notes: brown/cream wooden board, lichess-style cburnett pieces + custom dragon-head icons; webcam overlay, ~4-5 min clocks

setup: White: Ke1 + N dragons on the back rank (positions visual-only; e.g. 1 dragon on d1/c1 area). Black: full army rnbqkbnr/pppppppp. Board shown flipped in frames (dragon side at top).
events: +1 dragon after each loss; courtesy rematches where the GM takes the dragons
current_impl_issues: Impl kingplus A n=1 matches the setup but needs the auto-increment per loss up to 6 and a ~5-min clock; brown board theme.
evidence: 0:01-0:20 intro, 'dragon moves like a knight and a bishop'; 3:45 two dragons; 5:59 lose with two; 9:49 win with three; 15:47 'only 5 minutes'; 59:17 'defeat the grandmaster with six dragons'. Frame visual_a brown board, webcam, arturchix.
